g.text: CPython dict after d = {'cat': 1, 'dog': 2, 'emu': 3}: sparse index array plus dense entry array
dk_indices: the actual hash table, 8 slots of int8 while the table is small; -1 means empty
slot = hash(key) & 7; on a collision the probe sequence is perturbed by the high bits of the hash (slots here are illustrative)
dk_entries: dense and append only, one row per key; iterating the dict walks this array, which is why order is insertion order
lookup 'dog': slot 5 holds 1, so check entries[1]:
hash matches, key matches, return me_value = 2
8 int8 slots cost 8 bytes; a pointer per slot would cost 64
at most 2/3 of slots are ever used, then the table grows to 3 x used
a delete leaves DKIX_DUMMY (-2) in the slot and a NULL entry row
Constants from Objects/dictobject.c on CPython main, as of 2026-09-17.
